propositions: A configured provider is silently discarded when a model id contains a colon (e.g., versioned Bedrock ids like 'us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0'), because _resolve_target treats any colon as a provider-qualifier separator.
The bug affects only canonical versioned Bedrock model ids with the '-v1:0' suffix; unversioned aliases without colons work correctly.
When resolution fails, error messages report a fragment of the model id as the unknown provider, contradicting the operator's actual configuration.

The fix extracts the qualified/unqualified decision into a single shared function that validates whether a colon-separated prefix is a valid provider identifier, and checks configured providers before scanning the model string.
An explicitly configured provider must take priority over any inline qualifier in the model string; conflicting providers raise LLMConfigError at config-read time rather than silently discarding one.
